step1_figure.description: A high-speed rail-to-rail CMOS comparator composed of complementary PMOS and NMOS differential input stages, current summation into a positive-feedback decision circuit (M5-M8 with diode level shifter), and an output buffer consisting of a PMOS differential amplifier driving a CMOS inverter.

voltage_gain.description: DC small-signal voltage gain of the comparator (dVout/dVin) near the switching threshold

equation.explanation: Cascaded gain of the preamplifier differential pairs, the regenerative decision stage, and the output buffer/inverter.
equation.assumptions: Operating in the high-gain transition region with small differential input overdrive.

sky130_expected.calculation: Textbook reports ~175,000 (105 dB) for long-channel 5V CMOS. In Sky130 1.8V with short-channel effects and lower intrinsic transistor gain (ro), the cascaded gain across the three stages typically ranges from 5,000 to 50,000 (74 dB to 94 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Lower output impedance of submicron 1.8V FETs reduces per-stage gain compared to 5V legacy processes, yielding ~10k - 30k overall gain.

systematic_offset.description: Input-referred systematic offset voltage at common-mode voltage Vm = 0.9 V

equation.explanation: Difference between positive and negative inputs when the comparator output is halfway between rails.
equation.assumptions: Symmetric layout nominal conditions, systematic mismatch due to asymmetric loading of single-ended output buffer.

sky130_expected.calculation: Systematic offset shown in Fig 27.11 is under 1 mV. For balanced differential structures in Sky130, V_OS is typically within +/- 5 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Single-ended conversion in the PMOS output buffer diff-amp introduces a slight systematic offset.

hysteresis_voltage.description: Hysteresis width (switching point difference between high-going and low-going transitions)

equation.explanation: Switching trip points determined by the aspect ratio ratio beta_B / beta_A of the decision circuit cross-coupled pair. When beta_A = beta_B, hysteresis is zero.
equation.assumptions: Designed symmetrically with beta_A = beta_B (W5=W6=W7=W8) for zero nominal hysteresis.

sky130_expected.calculation: Since beta_A = beta_B (W5=W8=W6=W7=10u), beta_B / beta_A = 1, so V_H = 0 V theoretically, and < 2 mV in simulation.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Designed without intended hysteresis per text on page 916.

propagation_delay_lh.description: Propagation delay for a low-to-high output transition under 50 mV overdrive

equation.explanation: Time delay from the differential input crossing zero to the output reaching 50% VDD.
equation.assumptions: 50 mV input overdrive, 10 ns input transition.

sky130_expected.calculation: Textbook specifies ~9 ns for 5V CMOS. In Sky130 0.13um technology with lower parasitic capacitances, delay is substantially faster: typically 1.0 ns to 5.0 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sky130 transconductance is higher and junction capacitances are lower than legacy 1um/2um CMOS.

propagation_delay_hl.description: Propagation delay for a high-to-low output transition under 50 mV overdrive

equation.explanation: Time delay from negative-going differential input crossing zero to the output falling to 50% VDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: Similar to tpLH, typically 1.0 ns to 5.0 ns in 130 nm CMOS.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Slight difference between rise and fall delays occurs due to PMOS buffer asymmetric pull-up/pull-down drive.

supply_current.description: Total quiescent current drawn from VDD including bias circuitry

equation.formula: I_{DD} = I_{bias} + I_{SS,N} + I_{SS,P} + I_{decision} + I_{buffer}
equation.explanation: Sum of currents flowing through all branches from VDD to ground at nominal operating point.
equation.assumptions: Static DC operating point at mid-rail input (vp = vm = 0.9 V).

sky130_expected.calculation: With Iss ~ 40 uA per diff-pair, bias circuit ~ 30 uA, decision branch ~ 40 uA, buffer ~ 30 uA: I_total ~ 150 uA to 300 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Figure 27.10 shows ~240 uA at 5V; scaled to 1.8V with 6.5k bias resistor yields ~150-250 uA.

equation.explanation: Output rail-to-rail voltage provided by the CMOS output inverter xm14/xm15.
equation.assumptions: No external DC resistive load pulling down.

sky130_expected.reasoning: CMOS inverter drives to VDD when input is pulled low.

equation.explanation: Output rail-to-rail voltage provided by the CMOS output inverter xm14/xm15.
equation.assumptions: No external DC resistive load pulling up.

sky130_expected.reasoning: CMOS inverter pulls output completely to GND when input is high.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench measuring DC transfer characteristics, comparator gain, offset voltage, quiescent supply current, logic output levels, and transient propagation delays under 50 mV overdrive.
